title: Malicious admission controller
description: Admission controller is a Kubernetes component that intercepts, and possibly modifies, requests to the Kubernetes API server. There are two types of admissions controllers: validating and mutating controllers. As the name implies, a mutating admission controller can modify the intercepted request and change its properties. Kubernetes has a built-in generic admission controller named MutatingAdmissionWebhook. The behavior of this admission controller is determined by an admission webhook that the user deploys in the cluster. Attackers can use such webhooks for gaining persistence in the cluster. For example, attackers can intercept and modify the pod creation operations in the cluster and add their malicious container to every created pod.

data_components.name: Application Log Content
data_components.definition: Kubernetes API server audit log recording creation or modification of MutatingWebhookConfiguration and ValidatingWebhookConfiguration objects, which is the primary signal for malicious admission controller deployment.
relevant_events: Kubernetes audit event: verb in [create, update, patch], objectRef.apiGroup=admissionregistration.k8s.io, objectRef.resource=mutatingwebhookconfigurations
Kubernetes audit event: verb in [create, update, patch], objectRef.apiGroup=admissionregistration.k8s.io, objectRef.resource=validatingwebhookconfigurations
Kubernetes audit event: webhook configuration points to an external URL (clientConfig.url) outside cluster-internal namespace-based service references

data_components.name: Cluster Metadata
data_components.definition: Cluster-wide configuration state including the set of registered admission webhooks and their service endpoint bindings, used to establish a baseline and detect unauthorized additions.
relevant_events: Periodic audit of kubectl get mutatingwebhookconfigurations showing webhook rules with namespaceSelector or objectSelector matching all pods
New webhook registration with failurePolicy=Ignore (attacker uses this to avoid breaking the cluster while still intercepting requests)
Webhook clientConfig.service pointing to a namespace or service account not associated with any known service mesh or admission control product

data_components.name: Pod Modification
data_components.definition: Pod creation events where the admitted pod spec differs from the requested spec, indicating a mutating webhook has injected additional containers or modified security contexts without operator knowledge.
relevant_events: Kubernetes audit event: requestObject.spec.containers differs from responseObject.spec.containers for verb=create on pods (webhook mutation detected)
New container in pod spec not matching any known sidecar injector (e.g., not istio-proxy, vault-agent) after pod is scheduled
Kubernetes audit event: admission webhook call logged for pod creation where webhook adds containers[] entry with malicious image

detection_strategies.name: Behavioral Detection of Event Triggered Execution Across Platforms
detection_strategies.summary: T1546 is Event Triggered Execution; AN0027 covers cloud function creation triggered by audit log events. For K8s, the webhook registration IS the event trigger setup. The detection chain is: webhook configuration created/modified (audit log) + subsequent pod mutations observed.

vendor_detections.title: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration / MutatingWebhookConfiguration created or modified
vendor_detections.intent: Every change to admission webhook configuration. A malicious mutating webhook can rewrite every pod admitted to the cluster, granting persistence and instant-deploy-time tampering.
vendor_detections.query:
// Wiz Threat Center / Kubernetes Audit Log query (Resource Graph style)
KubernetesAuditLog
| where verb in ("create", "update", "patch", "replace")
  and objectRef.apiGroup == "admissionregistration.k8s.io"
  and objectRef.resource in ("validatingwebhookconfigurations", "mutatingwebhookconfigurations")
| project requestReceivedTimestamp,
          principal = user.username,
          name      = objectRef.name,
          kind      = objectRef.resource,
          webhooks  = requestObject.webhooks
required_telemetry: Audit policy at RequestResponse for admissionregistration.k8s.io
vendor_detections.false_positive_considerations: Legitimate operators (cert-manager, OPA Gatekeeper, Kyverno, Istio) install/update webhooks during their lifecycle. Allowlist by service-account-of-origin and by webhook name pattern.
vendor_detections.limitations: Sees the configuration change but not the malicious payload that runs at admission time. Pair with a Falco rule that tracks suspicious behavior of the webhook server pod itself.

vendor_detections.title: Falco: admission webhook configuration mutated by non-platform principal
vendor_detections.intent: Fire on every webhook configuration mutation by a principal that is not on the trusted-platform allowlist (cert-manager, OPA Gatekeeper, Kyverno, Istio operator).
vendor_detections.query:
- list: trusted_admission_principals
  items:
    - "system:serviceaccount:cert-manager:cert-manager"
    - "system:serviceaccount:gatekeeper-system:gatekeeper-admin"
    - "system:serviceaccount:kyverno:kyverno-admission-controller"
    - "system:serviceaccount:istio-system:istiod-service-account"

- rule: Admission Webhook Configuration Mutated
  desc: A validating or mutating webhook configuration was changed by a non-trusted principal.
  condition: kevt and (kcreate or kmodify)
             and ka.target.resource in ("validatingwebhookconfigurations", "mutatingwebhookconfigurations")
             and not (ka.user.name in (trusted_admission_principals))
  output: >
    Admission webhook config mutated
    (user=%ka.user.name verb=%ka.verb resource=%ka.target.resource
     name=%ka.target.name)
  priority: CRITICAL
  source: k8s_audit
  tags: [k8s, mitre_persistence, T1546]
required_telemetry: Audit policy at RequestResponse for admissionregistration.k8s.io
trusted_admission_principals list updated when new admission-controlling operators are installed
vendor_detections.false_positive_considerations: Operator upgrades that re-create webhook configurations under a different SA fire here until the allowlist is updated. Bias toward alert-not-block until tuned.
vendor_detections.limitations: No visibility into the webhook payload itself. A webhook that legitimately exists but starts behaving maliciously (e.g., via an updated container image) is invisible to this rule.

vendor_detections.title: Webhook configuration change history with rare-principal anomaly
vendor_detections.intent: List every webhook configuration change in the lake; flag those by principals that have not changed webhook configuration in the prior 90 days as anomalous.
vendor_detections.query:
WITH webhook_changes AS (
  SELECT
    event_time,
    cluster_name,
    user_username AS principal,
    object_resource AS kind,
    object_name AS name,
    verb,
    request_object
  FROM K8S_AUDIT.PUBLIC.EVENTS
  WHERE verb IN ('create', 'update', 'patch', 'replace')
    AND object_resource IN ('validatingwebhookconfigurations', 'mutatingwebhookconfigurations')
    AND object_apigroup = 'admissionregistration.k8s.io'
    AND event_time >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())
),
principal_history AS (
  SELECT
    user_username AS principal,
    MAX(event_time) AS last_seen_before_window
  FROM K8S_AUDIT.PUBLIC.EVENTS
  WHERE object_resource IN ('validatingwebhookconfigurations', 'mutatingwebhookconfigurations')
    AND event_time < DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())
    AND event_time >= DATEADD(day, -97, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  c.*,
  CASE WHEN h.last_seen_before_window IS NULL THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS new_principal
FROM   webhook_changes c
LEFT JOIN principal_history h ON h.principal = c.principal
ORDER  BY new_principal DESC, event_time DESC;
required_telemetry: K8s audit logs landed in Snowflake with at least 97 days retention
Audit policy capturing admissionregistration.k8s.io at RequestResponse
vendor_detections.false_positive_considerations: First-time installs of legitimate admission operators flag here. Combine with vendor reputation lookup or a manual approval workflow on first-seen principals.
vendor_detections.limitations: 90-day baseline assumes the lake retains audit logs that long. Adjust window to your retention.

mitre_cross_references.name: Valid Accounts
mitre_cross_references.rationale: The Sigma rule 'kubernetes_audit_change_admission_controller' (and its identical GCP/Azure variants) tags T1078 alongside T1552.007. Creating or modifying a webhook admission controller requires cluster-admin privileges; the attacker must first authenticate with valid credentials (T1078) to reach the admissionregistration.k8s.io API endpoint. This precondition is documented in both the Sigma rule description ('can be used by an adversary to achieve persistence or exfiltrate access credentials') and the reference to a Padok security blog post.

mitre_cross_references.name: Container API
mitre_cross_references.rationale: The Sigma rule 'kubernetes_audit_change_admission_controller' is tagged both T1078 and T1552.007. A malicious admission controller intercepts every pod creation request and can extract secrets from pod specs, environment variables, and volume mounts as they pass through -- the credential-exfiltration objective maps to T1552.007 (Container API credential read). The rule description explicitly states: 'exfiltrate access credentials' as an objective.
